title: PRD: deterministic envelope sequencing and backpressure behavior for incremental function outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines acceptance criteria and scope for a deterministic framing/envelope protocol for streamed structured output that interacts with tool/function-calling subsystems. It clarifies how incremental JSON frames are sequenced, how the system signals and handles backpressure from downstream tool gateways, and the error classification and fallback semantics when parts of a stream fail. The goal is to reduce ambiguity for SDKs and integrators and ensure graceful, observable behavior in production workloads.
background: Multiple PM and ENG tickets surfaced inconsistent behavior during partial-stream failure modes and tool gateway saturation. Integrations observed out-of-order frame injection, duplicate tool invocations, and unclear retry boundaries when an intermediate frame fails validation. This PRD captures a deterministic approach used by runtime/SDKs to avoid these issues and specifies telemetry and acceptance tests.
scope: In scope: envelope sequence numbers, checkpoint acknowledgements, per-frame schema validation policy, backpressure signals (flow control), idempotent function-call semantics, explicit fallback modes (best-effort vs fail-stop), telemetry instrumentation, e2e test harnesses. Out of scope: changing existing function call API surface, global auth/permission model, heavy-weight encryption changes.
out_of_scope: Non-streamed batch-only function invocation redesign; SDK language-specific ergonomics beyond minimal glue; full rewrite of runtime buffer manager.
acceptance_criteria: Every emitted structured frame must include an envelope with: unique envelope_id, frame_seq (monotonic integer per request), and optional checkpoint_tag. SDKs and runtime must accept frames only when frame_seq increments by exactly 1 (no silent reordering).

If a frame is rejected by the downstream tool gateway due to schema validation, the runtime returns a framed ERROR object for that frame_seq with error_class set to 'schema' or 'recoverable' as appropriate; the stream remains open unless the error_class is 'fatal'.

Backpressure signal: when a tool gateway returns HTTP 429 or an equivalent flow-control signal, the runtime must emit a SYSTEM_FLOW_CONTROL envelope to the client stream within 50ms and hold further tool invocations for that request for up to 5s while keeping application frames buffered and ordered. Documentation must specify exponential backoff behavior for retries.

Idempotency: each function/tool invocation must be associated with an idempotency_key derived from envelope_id + frame_seq. Retries triggered by transient errors (network, 5xx, flow control) must not cause duplicated side-effects for invocations that report success. Acceptance test will validate exactly-once semantics for simulated tool that records side-effects.

Streaming partial JSON: clients must be able to receive and parse partial, incremental JSON objects when frames include 'partial=true'. The runtime will include clear 'final=true' marker for completion of a logical object. Parsers must be able to recover from intermediate non-final frames and not treat them as parse errors. E2E tests will demonstrate recovery from an interrupted stream and successful resume from last checkpoint.

Fallback modes: product must provide two documented fallback modes: 'graceful-degrade' (skip tool invocation and include a diagnostic envelope explaining missing tool result) and 'fail-fast' (terminate stream with a FATAL envelope). The PRD includes criteria for choosing default mode based on customer SLA tier and request route configuration.

Observability: every frame must emit metrics/trace tags including envelope_id, frame_seq, tool_id, invocation_status (queued, sent, success, fail, retried), and backpressure_events. There must be dashboards showing per-route percent of frames that hit flow-control and average requeue latency. Acceptance requires dashboard with synthetic workload demonstrating behavior.

Contract testing: provide schema-based unit tests that exercise: valid frame flow, frame validation failure handling, reordering attempt (should be rejected), and simultaneous multi-tool fan-out (ensure per-tool ordering). All tests must be automated in CI and pass on the release branch.

Latency SLOs: when no flow control is applied, first structural frame (first byte of a structured object) must be emitted to client within 150ms for 95th percentile on synthetic workload. When backpressure occurs, the system must surface the SYSTEM_FLOW_CONTROL envelope within 50ms as noted above. Regression checks will be in CI perf suite.
success_metrics: <1% of production streams experience out-of-order frame rejection after rollout (measured over 7d)
>99.5% of transient tool invocation retries do not produce duplicate side-effects in simulated replay tests
Dashboards present flow-control signal rate and mean retry latency by route
E2E CI runs for structured stream tests succeed on release branch for 3 consecutive runs before ship
test_cases: Simulate schema rejection mid-stream: ensure ERROR envelope emitted, stream remains open, subsequent frames accepted if schema corrected by model and labeled final when complete
Induce tool gateway 429: confirm SYSTEM_FLOW_CONTROL envelope and exponential backoff; no out-of-order frames accepted during backpressure period
Replay idempotency test: send identical envelope pairs; assert single side-effect in tool harness
Network partition resume: cut TCP after frame N, reconnect, resume must pick up at checkpoint_tag N and not replay frames before checkpoint
implementation_notes: Runtime: add envelope parser/validator that enforces monotonic frame_seq and emits ERROR/FATAL envelopes. Tool gateway client: add idempotency-key header and flow-control handler that converts 429 into SYSTEM_FLOW_CONTROL with backoff guidance. SDKs: expose checkpoint ACK API and a 'resume_from' helper. Ensure compatibility layer maps older non-enveloped streams to default envelope with seq starting at 1 for backward compatibility.
tradeoffs: Tight sequencing increases runtime complexity and may add latency for high-concurrency requests; we mitigate with per-request lightweight indexing rather than global locks. Idempotency requires coordination with tool adapters and may not be possible for third-party tools without idempotency support; in that case we fall back to conservative 'graceful-degrade' by default.
open_questions: Should checkpoint_tag be opaque or human-readable? (engineering preference: opaque GUID for uniqueness)
Default fallback mode for hosted customers vs enterprise customers? (proposal: hosted -> graceful-degrade, enterprise -> configurable)
Do we extend idempotency guarantees outside our tool adapter boundary for partner integrations?
